description: Media inspection library and agreement/delivery API routes. Install sharp for image inspection, create graceful video inspection with ffprobe fallback. Implement POST /api/agreements (create from accepted proposal), GET /api/agreements/[id], POST /api/agreements/[id]/accept (creator/brand acceptance), POST /api/deliveries (upload with automatic inspection), GET /api/deliveries, GET /api/deliveries/[id] (signed download URL).
steps: Install sharp: npm install sharp --save. Verify package.json lists sharp in dependencies after install.

Create lib/mediaInspector.ts with types: InspectionCheck { requirement: string, actual: string, expected: string, passed: boolean }, InspectionResult { status: 'pass'|'fail'|'unsupported'|'error', checks: InspectionCheck[], metadata: Record<string,any>, message?: string }. Export async function inspectMedia(filePath: string, requirements: any): Promise<InspectionResult>.

Implement inspectImage in lib/mediaInspector.ts using sharp: sharp(filePath).metadata() to get width, height, format. Calculate aspect ratio as width/height. Compare with requirements.aspectRatios (convert '9:16' to 9/16=0.5625). Tolerance: aspect ratio ±1% (Math.abs(actual - expected) / expected < 0.01). Return pass/fail with checks array showing each requirement.

Implement inspectVideo in lib/mediaInspector.ts: Try to import 'fluent-ffmpeg' dynamically - if import fails OR ffprobe not found, return {status: 'unsupported', message: 'Video inspection requires ffprobe (not available in this environment)'}. If available, use ffmpeg.ffprobe(filePath) to get duration, width, height, fps, codec. Compare duration (tolerance ±0.5s), resolution (exact match), aspect ratio (±1%). 30-second timeout. Catch errors and return status='error' with error message.

Implement main inspectMedia function: Check file extension - if jpg/jpeg/png/webp, call inspectImage. If mp4/mov/webm, call inspectVideo. Otherwise return {status: 'unsupported', message: 'File format not supported'}. Wrap all in try-catch returning status='error' on exceptions.

Create types/index.ts additions: Add Agreement interface (id, briefId, proposalId, creatorId, brandId, version, deliverables, price, currency, milestones, includedRevisions, usageRequirements, creatorAcceptedAt, brandAcceptedAt, createdAt, updatedAt), Delivery interface (id, agreementId, creatorId, version, filePath, fileName, fileSizeBytes, mimeType, inspectionStatus, inspectionResults, inspectedAt, brandApprovedAt, approvalNotes, createdAt), ProjectMessage interface (id, agreementId, senderId, messageType, content, deliveryVersion, videoTimestampSeconds, proposedChanges, changeAcceptedByCreator, changeAcceptedByBrand, createdAt).

Create app/api/agreements/route.ts POST: (1) Get authenticated user via supabase.auth.getUser(). (2) Get proposalId from request body. (3) Fetch proposal with brief data, verify proposal.status='Accepted'. (4) Verify user is either the brand (owns brief) or creator (owns proposal). (5) Check no agreement exists yet for this proposal: SELECT FROM agreements WHERE proposal_id=X. (6) Extract deliverables from brief (contentType, aspectRatios, durationSeconds, resolution, quantity), milestones from proposal (timelineDays), price from proposal. (7) Insert agreement with version=1, creator_accepted_at=null, brand_accepted_at=null. Return 201 with agreement object.

Create app/api/agreements/[id]/route.ts GET: (1) Verify authenticated. (2) Fetch agreement with creator and brand user_id joined. (3) Verify request user is participant (creator's user_id OR brand's user_id). (4) Return agreement with full history - later can extend to return all versions, for now return single version.

Create app/api/agreements/[id]/accept/route.ts POST: (1) Verify authenticated. (2) Fetch agreement with creator/brand user_id. (3) Verify user is participant. (4) Determine if user is creator or brand based on user_id match. (5) If creator, update creator_accepted_at=NOW(). If brand, update brand_accepted_at=NOW(). (6) Check if both_accepted became true - if yes, update brief status to 'In Production' (new status, add to BriefStatus type). Return 200 with updated agreement.

Create lib/storage.ts for Supabase Storage helpers: async function uploadDelivery(agreementId: string, file: File): Promise<{path: string, error?: string}>. Create path as deliveries/{agreementId}/{version}_{timestamp}_{filename}. Use createClient().storage.from('deliveries').upload(path, file). Return path on success.

Create app/api/deliveries/route.ts POST: (1) Verify authenticated user. (2) Parse multipart/form-data to get file and agreementId from request. Use request.formData(). (3) Fetch agreement, verify user is creator. (4) Validate file: max 500MB (500 * 1024 * 1024 bytes), check actual MIME type using file-type library or file.type. (5) Determine next version number: SELECT MAX(version) FROM deliveries WHERE agreement_id=X, increment. (6) Upload to storage using lib/storage.ts. (7) Save file locally to temp dir for inspection. (8) Call inspectMedia with agreement.deliverables as requirements. (9) Insert delivery record with inspection results. (10) Delete temp file. Return 201 with delivery object including inspection results.
Create app/api/deliveries/route.ts GET: Query param agreementId. Verify user is participant of that agreement. Return deliveries array ordered by version DESC.

Create app/api/deliveries/[id]/route.ts GET: (1) Fetch delivery with agreement, verify user is participant. (2) Use supabase.storage.from('deliveries').createSignedUrl(delivery.filePath, 3600) to create 1-hour signed download URL. (3) Return {url: signedUrl, fileName: delivery.fileName, mimeType: delivery.mimeType}.
acceptance_criteria: sharp installed and listed in package.json dependencies
lib/mediaInspector.ts exports inspectMedia function with correct type signatures
Image inspection works for jpg/png/webp: extracts dimensions, aspect ratio, compares with requirements, returns pass/fail with tolerance ±1%
Video inspection gracefully falls back when ffprobe unavailable: returns status='unsupported' with clear message, never false pass
POST /api/agreements creates agreement from accepted proposal, requires authenticated participant, returns 400 if proposal not accepted or agreement already exists
POST /api/agreements/[id]/accept updates correct acceptance timestamp (creator vs brand), prevents non-participants from accepting, updates brief status when both accepted
POST /api/deliveries validates file size (max 500MB), uploads to private storage, runs inspection, saves results, returns delivery with inspection status
GET /api/deliveries/[id] returns signed URL with 1-hour expiry, only accessible to agreement participants
All routes return 401 for unauthenticated, 403 for non-participants, 404 for missing resources
verification: Build check: npm run build. Verify 0 TypeScript errors (may show prerender warnings - acceptable).

Test POST /api/agreements: Use Postman or curl with valid session cookie, accepted proposal ID from database. Expect 201 response with agreement object containing version=1, both acceptance timestamps null. Verify in Supabase: SELECT * FROM agreements WHERE proposal_id='<id>'. Expect 1 row.

Test POST /api/agreements/[id]/accept: Call with creator session, then brand session. After both, verify both_accepted=true in database. Verify brief status updated to 'Hired' (existing) or 'In Production' in briefs table.

Test media inspection locally: Create test image (9:16, 1080x1920), call inspectMedia with requirements {aspectRatios: ['9:16'], resolution: '1080x1920'}. Expect status='pass'. Test with wrong aspect ratio (16:9 image vs 9:16 requirement). Expect status='fail' with checks showing mismatch.

Test POST /api/deliveries: Use form-data with file (mp4 or jpg) and agreementId. Verify file uploaded to Supabase Storage at deliveries/{agreementId}/{version}_*. Verify delivery row in database with inspection_status='pass'/'fail'/'unsupported'. Check inspection_results JSONB contains checks array.
Test GET /api/deliveries/[id]: Verify returns signed URL, download works in browser, expires after 1 hour, returns 403 for non-participant user.
